A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LIFT research work despite substantial redesign. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison; graphical text extraction problems were resolved through visual inspection.

before.justification: v3 reports original LooGLE and LongBench evaluations, efficiency measurements, NIAH experiments, ablations, and attention-output analyses.

after.justification: v4 reports original SQuAD, NIAH, and LooGLE experiments, efficiency measurements, qualitative analyses, and general-capability evaluations in Appendix G.

M1.justification: v3 combines contextualized segment memorization and auxiliary QA training with a Gated Memory adapter and truncated-context inference. v4's standard method instead trains LoRA solely on synthetic QA pairs and supplies no document context during inference. It generates multiple QAs per sentence and introduces asynchronous generation/training. Segmented language modeling and truncated ICL remain experimental variants in Appendix H, rather than standard components.

E1.justification: LooGLE and NIAH are retained. v4 adds SQuAD comprehension experiments and MMLU, GSM8K, and ARC Challenge capability evaluations. v3's five-task LongBench evaluation, including QMSum and GovReport summarization, is no longer reported, despite residual LongBench mentions in v4's baseline appendix. This substantially changes the evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: v4 adds MemoryLLM, LlamaIndex, TempLoRA, LLMLingua, and Finetune-Raw to the LooGLE comparison, plus LLoCO in Appendix D; v3's PiSSA comparison disappears. Within NIAH, full-context ICL is replaced by Finetune-Raw as the comparator. Figure 4 additionally compares against a borrowed SEAL score, explicitly attributed to its source rather than presented as a reproduction.

E3.justification: For Llama-3/LooGLE, v3 reports a 1e-3 learning rate and 3+5 training epochs; v4 reports 5e-5 and five epochs under its revised training design. Backbone evaluations add Qwen 3 and Llama 2 and drop GPT-3.5. NIAH's length/depth grid and efficiency-testing settings change. Appendix D introduces a random LooGLE train/test split for LLoCO, although Table 7's QuALITY caption conflicts with that description and its task columns.

E4.justification: v3's contextualized-training and Gated Memory ablations, in-/out-context breakdown, and attention-similarity diagnostic disappear. v4 adds a manually classified SQuAD error analysis, asynchronous-pipeline ablation, general-capability retention tests, and segmented-LM/truncated-ICL combination experiments. QA-count sensitivity changes from counts per document to counts per sentence. These substantially revise the questions investigated and supporting evidence.

E5.justification: v4 explicitly reports averaging capability metrics over ten independently document-fine-tuned models in Appendix G, adding model-run and aggregation information absent from v3. These are adaptations to different documents, not identified random-seed replications. Neither version reports dispersion, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 reports Llama-3 LIFT ShortQA/LongQA scores of 47.51/29.97 using Gated Memory and truncated ICL; v4 reports 52.69/27.25 for its QA-only LoRA configuration. These are differently configured results, while the corresponding truncated-ICL scores remain 44.49/15.44. v4 adds SQuAD results, 100% NIAH accuracy under its revised setup, capability scores, and new comparison/variant results; LongBench results disappear.

T1.justification: v3's Gated Memory attention decomposition, gate and memory definitions, and approximation argument in Section 3.4 are removed, along with the contextualized-training formalism. v4 retains the QA likelihood objective in equivalent form and adds a short complexity comparison between multiple short QAs and one long QA. The mathematical substance is substantially reduced and redirected.

C1.justification: The overarching claim of storing long-input knowledge in parameters remains. However, Gated Memory's balance between memorization and ICL is removed as a central contribution. v4 instead foregrounds synthetic-QA comprehension and asynchronous adaptation, adding explicit claims of sub-10-second TTFT for 8K inputs and perfect NIAH accuracy.

C2.justification: v3 emphasizes the memorization-versus-ICL tradeoff, difficulty extracting parametric knowledge, and Gated Memory's failure to reproduce full-context attention. v4 develops a different explanation centered on raw-text pattern matching versus explicit QA knowledge. Its limitations focus on sentence-level coverage failing to improve document-wide information association. Appendix G newly interprets capability scores as preservation rather than improved general intelligence.

D1.justification: v4 documents LoRA rank and initialization, revised generator prompts, Qwen2.5-72B deployment through vLLM, multi-GPU training, and baseline reproduction procedures, and supplies an implementation link. These replace much of v3's two-stage training documentation. v3's optimizer/decoding settings and GPU-hour table are not retained; reported hardware changes from a single A800 to A100/H20 clusters.

R1.justification: v4 adds substantial positioning around memory-augmented models and synthetic data, discussing methods including MemoryLLM, SEAL, InfiniteICL, Genie, and TTT-E2E. The distinction from earlier test-time training shifts from the Gated Memory adapter to synthetic-QA comprehension and efficient deployment. This materially revises the novelty argument, beyond updating citations.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method exposition, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Section 3 changes from segmentation, contextualized training, and adapter derivation to motivation, synthetic-task generation, and pipeline design. The experiment narrative and appendices are reorganized, and the separate limitations section is replaced by different discussion in the conclusion.

P2.justification: v4 redraws the overview and removes the segmentation, Gated Memory architecture, and attention-similarity graphics. It adds error-analysis, pipeline, and SQuAD displays, redesigns the NIAH heatmaps and efficiency plots, and restructures the LooGLE tables. Table 1 is transposed and changes comparison criteria. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens support for parameter-based answering through explicit document-free evaluation, broader method comparisons, and capability-retention checks (Table 3; Appendices G–H), improving on v3's main reliance on LIFT plus truncated ICL. Detailed generation and baseline recipes also help assessment. These benefits are tempered by removal of LongBench evidence while summarization benefits remain claimed, and by changed hardware/settings that prevent interpreting efficiency results as matched improvements.
